description: A ₹26,910-crore data centre and AI hub is planned in Jewar, UP, with Phase-I capacity of 384 MW targeted for 2028.
body_lead: Lucknow: Uttar Pradesh is set to strengthen its digital infrastructure with a ₹26,910-crore data centre and artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure hub in Jewar, with the first phase planned to have a capacity of 384 MW. The project, being developed by AM Group in Sector 28 of the Yamuna Expressway Industrial Development Authority (YEIDA) area, will cover 114 acres. The first phase is targeted for commissioning in 2028 and forms part of a larger plan to establish a 1 GW high-performance computing and AI infrastructure hub by 2030.
